Ballon d'Or London Ceremony Marred by Logistics and Security Disruptions

02 Nov 2026, 02:26 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Image: https://www.facebook.com/BBCSport/ · Source image rights not independently verified · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9 for the website

Overview of the Event

The recent Ballon d'Or ceremony, held for the first time in its 70-year history at the London Palladium, faced significant logistical and security challenges that delayed the proceedings. While the event saw Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas emerge as the primary award winners, the evening was characterized by crowd control issues and administrative errors.

Key Disruptions

  • Traffic and Access: The ceremony start was delayed by 45 minutes due to heavy congestion in central London, exacerbated by a traffic-free initiative on nearby Oxford Street and unexpected crowd sizes.
  • Crowd Control: Large numbers of fans gathered outside the venue, leading to the scaling and removal of metal barriers. The Metropolitan Police issued a Section 35 dispersal order and reported that some individuals threw objects at officers. Two arrests were made during the evening.
  • Ceremonial Conduct: Inside the venue, hosts experienced difficulty managing a boisterous audience, leading to several pauses in the program. Additionally, reports surfaced regarding a lack of diversity in the press conference for Harry Kane, where female journalists were reportedly ignored during the Q&A session.

Administrative and Communication Issues

Concerns regarding the integrity of the results arose before the event when the official Ballon d'Or website inadvertently published articles declaring multiple nominees, including Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé, and Alexia Putellas, as winners. A spokesperson stated these were pre-prepared templates and not indications of results. A subsequent social media post also erroneously conflated the names of female nominees, for which the organizers have faced criticism.

Official Response

Organizers issued an apology regarding the security failures, noting that fan turnout far exceeded initial projections. The Metropolitan Police confirmed they assisted with crowd management, ensuring the safety of officers and the public during the dispersal of the crowds.

To verify official details and future updates regarding these events, observers should consult the official Ballon d'Or website and statements released via their verified media channels.
